claims.text: The feedstock is pre-alloyed AlCrFeNiSi powder suitable for high-energy LPBF deposition.
The proposed intervention is integrated in-situ induction heating that maintains the substrate and build area at approximately 200°C during deposition.
A controlled or inert atmosphere will prevent oxidation during induction-heated LPBF.
The induction system continuously preheats the substrate and deposited layers.
Maintaining the build near 200°C will reduce thermal gradients and rapid temperature swings during laser exposure.
Lower thermal gradients lessen thermal-contraction mismatch and thereby reduce residual thermal stress.
Reduced thermal gradients promote more uniform grain formation.
The controlled thermal profile promotes a refined and uniform microstructure.
Conventional LPBF subjects material to high thermal gradients and rapid cooling.
The thermal history of conventional LPBF produces residual stresses.
Conventional high-thermal-load LPBF degrades mechanical properties.
Conventional high-thermal-load LPBF has increased processing complexity.
Induction-heated AlCrFeNiSi components will have lower residual stresses than conventionally processed components.
Induction-heated AlCrFeNiSi components will have greater grain uniformity than conventionally processed components.
Induction-heated AlCrFeNiSi components will exhibit higher yield strength than conventionally processed components.
Induction-heated AlCrFeNiSi components will exhibit better ductility and elongation than conventionally processed components.
Integrating induction heating will simplify processing complexity relative to conventional high-thermal-load regimes.
The proposed processing window applies to miniature LPBF geometries at a build temperature around 200°C.
Extrapolation to substantially larger components or other alloy systems requires further validation.
Prior empirical data on in-situ induction heating of AlCrFeNiSi are limited, leaving the magnitude of the effects uncertain.
